blocks.text: Episode 136 opens by insisting that even after terrible losses the Khalsa remained inexhaustible, because Sikh bands kept re-forming wherever pressure fell hardest. Families were hidden in Malwa while armed Singhs continued to strike opportunistically, refusing to let persecution extinguish the Panth.

The page emphasizes that mobility itself became a weapon: the Singhs kept plundering the vanguard and the rearguard day and night, forcing larger armies to feel hunted even when they believed themselves in command. This combination of concealment for families and relentless harassment by fighters explains why the Khalsa seemed impossible to finish off.

Abdali then lashes out symbolically as well as militarily by moving against Amritsar and violating the holy Harmandar Sahib and its sacred pool. Yet even this desecration is narrated not as final triumph, but as another act of rage in a struggle he still cannot conclusively end.
